title: Cofinality of the apex projection for cocones in a filtered quasicategory
statement:
Use universes, smallness, regular cardinals and filteredness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent cocone categories, simplicial pullbacks and weak contractibility of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa$ be an infinite regular cardinal, let $E$ be a small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory, let $K$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set and let $p:K\to E$ be a coherent diagram. Put $T=E_{p/}$ and let $V:T\to E$ be the apex projection. Then $T$ is small and $\kappa$-filtered. For every $e\in E$, form the coherent comma quasicategory
$$(e\downarrow V)=\{e\}\times_{E,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,E}T.$$
There is an equivalence $(e\downarrow V)\simeq E_{(p\amalg e)/}$ compatible with apex projections, where $p\amalg e:K\amalg\Delta^0\to E$ restricts to $p$ and to $e$. Consequently every $(e\downarrow V)$ is $\kappa$-filtered and weakly contractible, so $V$ satisfies the cofinal comma criterion. No colimit-existence hypothesis on $E$ is imposed, and $K=\varnothing$ is allowed.

proof.text: The coherent cocone category T is the simplicial pullback specified in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Since E and K are small, the simplicial set Fun(K,E), the arrow simplicial set Fun(Δ¹,Fun(K,E)), and the displayed pullback are small in the chosen universe; the same definition supplies its coherent higher simplices. Thus T is small, and V is the pullback projection recording the apex.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.5.15, setup of the cocone category; size bookkeeping expanded from the definitions

proof.text: Apply the filtered-coslice assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-coslice-calculus] with D=E, τ=κ and the κ-small diagram p. Its first assertion says that D_{p/} is κ-filtered whenever D is κ-filtered and the indexing simplicial set is κ-small. Therefore T=E_{p/} is κ-filtered (including the empty indexing shape).

source.place: Proposition 5.4.5.15, filteredness of the cocone category

proof.text: Use the degreewise pullback model of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and write D=Fun(K,E). An n-simplex of T is a pair (a,b), where a:Δ^n→E and b:Δ^n×Δ¹→D has initial endpoint constant at p and final endpoint Δ_K a. An n-simplex of (e↓V) adds c:Δ^n×Δ¹→E with initial endpoint constant at e and final endpoint a. Since (K⨿Δ⁰)×Δ^m=(K×Δ^m)⨿Δ^m in each degree m, restriction gives a simplicial isomorphism Fun(K⨿Δ⁰,E)=D×E. Under it the constant-diagram map is a↦(Δ_K a,a), and p⨿e corresponds to (p,e). The pair (b,c) is therefore exactly a map Δ^n×Δ¹→Fun(K⨿Δ⁰,E) from the constant p⨿e to the constant-diagram image of a. Thus (a,b,c)↦(a,(b,c)) and the inverse coordinate projections identify the comma pullback with E_{(p⨿e)/}. These inverse maps commute with every simplicial operator because all operators are restrictions on the same three coordinates. They fix a, hence respect the apex projection. This is a simplicial isomorphism, in particular the required functor equivalence.

source.place: Agent argument from the explicit coherent cocone pullback definition; coordinate splitting for a disjoint union, serving the final cofinality argument of HTT Proposition 5.4.5.15

proof.text: The coproduct K⨿Δ⁰ is κ-small because κ is infinite and K is κ-small. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-coslice-calculus] again to the κ-filtered quasicategory E and the diagram p⨿e shows that E_{(p⨿e)/} is κ-filtered. The equivalence in the preceding step therefore transfers κ-filteredness to every (e↓V).

source.place: Proposition 5.4.5.15, filteredness after adjoining one object

proof.text: Every small κ-filtered quasicategory is weakly contractible by the explicit filteredness consequence in [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula]. Thus each coherent comma quasicategory (e↓V), already shown κ-filtered, is weakly contractible.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1 together with Proposition 5.4.5.15, contractibility of filtered comma categories

proof.text: To check that the strict comma used above computes the homotopy comma of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion], put S_e={e}×_{E,ev_0}Fun(Δ¹,E) and t=ev_1:S_e→E. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration] to the quasicategory E^op and the vertex e. Reversing the vertex order of every simplex identifies Fun(Δ¹,E^op) with Fun(Δ¹,E)^op and exchanges ev_0 with ev_1, since the reversal of Δ¹×Δ^n is Δ¹×Δ^n with both factors reversed. Under it the node's E_e and its source evaluation become S_e^op and t^op. Reversal exchanges the horns Λ^m_j and Λ^m_{m-j}, so t lifts every Λ^m_j with m≥1 and 0≤j<m: t is a left fibration in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. S_e is a quasicategory: fill an inner horn of S_e first in E after applying t, then lift the filler along t. S_e is small, being a simplicial subset of the small Fun(Δ¹,E). By [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift], t is an isofibration in the sense of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]: it lifts inner horns, and equivalence edges with prescribed source to equivalence edges of S_e. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] to the isofibration t and the functor V:T→E. The degreewise pullback T×_E S_e, which is exactly the comma (e↓V), is a quasicategory and is the infinity-categorical pullback T×^h_E S_e required by the criterion. Thus the comma categories of the cited cofinal criterion are weakly contractible by step 5, and that criterion applies to V. This proves the asserted cofinal comma condition (and its colimit-cofinality consequence). No colimit in E has been assumed; K=∅ is included.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1 (cofinal comma criterion), applied to V; the coslice projection S_e→E is used as a left fibration, hence an isofibration, through the cited DAG nodes
